title.narrative: Improving resilience of vulnerable coastal communities & mangrove ecosystems

description.narrative: Active

Guyana’s coastal regions are home to a significant portion of the population, and they face increasing threats from climate change, including rising sea levels and coastal erosion. The “Coastal Resilience & Mangrove Restoration Project” was launched in September 2024 as part of a collaborative effort between GGGI, NAREI, and other national stakeholders. This initiative aims to enhance coastal resilience by restoring and preserving critical mangrove ecosystems, thereby protecting vulnerable communities and supporting the sustainability goals outlined in Guyana’s Low Carbon Development Strategy (LCDS) and National Mangrove Action Plan 2022-2032.

The project objective is to protect, expand and sustainably manage the mangrove ecosystems in Guyana and to maximize the services they provide to the local communities in support of the global fight against climate change. The project aims to achieve four main objectives: 1: Pilot green-grey solution in a 6km coastline and to prepare a plan to scale-up green-grey solutions. 2: Strengthen institutional capacity for mangroves management in Guyana. 3: Increase stakeholders and public awareness on of mangrove ecosystem services
